doc.summary: xhci.c -- xHCI host controller driver, polled event ring.
---- Register-space layout ----
doc.description:
Four windows, and mixing them up produces a driver that reads plausible
values and silently writes them nowhere:

  0x0000            capability registers (CAPLENGTH, HCSPARAMS, ...)
  CAPLENGTH         operational registers
  0x1000            runtime registers and the interrupter array
  0x2000            doorbell array

The operational window starts at CAPLENGTH, not at a fixed offset, and the
capability block is read-only: writing USBCMD at offset 0 lands in
CAPLENGTH, is dropped, and the controller never runs -- a failure that
looks like dead hardware rather than a wrong address.

These are the xHCI 1.x register offsets, not a private layout.

The interrupter array starts 0x20 into the runtime window, one 0x20 entry
per interrupter, and one interrupter is all this driver uses.

---- DMA alignment ----
doc.description:
64 bytes, and this is not alignment for its own sake: the hardware masks
the low bits of DCBAAP, of the command ring configuration register and of
the event ring segment table base. A ring allocated on 16 bytes and handed
over silently moves, and the controller then reads a command ring full of
zeros -- which looks exactly like a controller that ignores the doorbell.

Contexts need 32 and the context array 64, so one alignment covers every
structure the controller walks.

doc.summary: Docstring: Service the event ring.
doc.description: Drains every pending TRB and completes the matching transfer. Safe to call from any context, any number of times, with interrupts on or off; it allocates nothing and takes no lock. Returns 1 when it completed something.

doc.summary: Docstring: Stop, reset and re-point one endpoint's transfer ring after a stall or a timeout, so Bulk-Only recovery continues on the same ring.
doc.description: Returns 1 when the endpoint is usable again.

Docstring: Read a root port's live state.
doc.description: Returns 1 on a valid port number, 0 otherwise, and leaves out zeroed on refusal.

doc.summary: Docstring: Ask a port to reset, and wait for it to settle.
doc.description: Per spec the reset bit is PORTSC bit 4: set it with the W1C change bits written clear, then wait for PED set and PR clear. Returns 1 on a connected device.

name: xhc_open_interface
signature: int xhc_open_interface(int index, unsigned cls, unsigned sub, unsigned proto, xhc_iface_t *out)

doc.summary: Docstring: Find an interface of an enumerated device by class triple and copy out its endpoints.
doc.description:
A pure function over the cached configuration descriptor, with every
descriptor's bLength, type and remaining span checked before use: an
unterminated or zero-length descriptor ends the walk instead of looping,
and the endpoint count is capped by XHC_MAX_EPS. out is zeroed first, so
a caller that ignores the result sees a zeroed interface, never stale
stack. Returns 1 on a match with at least one endpoint, 0 otherwise.

doc.summary: ---- Control transfers ----
Docstring: USB is lossy and emulated controllers occasionally drop a completion, so a control transfer retries its whole setup-data-status stage up to three times before reporting failure.
doc.description: A stall or a refused stage is not retried: only a missing or failed completion is.

doc.summary: Docstring: USB is lossy and emulated controllers occasionally drop a completion, so a control transfer retries its whole setup-data-status stage up to three times before reporting failure.
doc.description: A stall or a refused * stage is not retried: only a missing or failed completion is. define XHC_CONTROL_TRIES 3u

name: xhc_configure_endpoint
signature: int xhc_configure_endpoint(int index, int ep_index, int ep_addr, int ep_type, int max_packet, int mult, int interval, int burst)

doc.summary: Docstring: Configure one non-control endpoint and give it a transfer ring. ep_index is the endpoint context index, 1..XHC_EP_INDEX_LIMIT-1. ep_addr carries the address and direction bits.
doc.description: Returns 1 on success, 0 on a bad index, a device that is not addressed, or an allocation failure.

name: xhc_transfer
signature: int xhc_transfer(int index, int ep_index, void *buf, unsigned len, int *got)

doc.summary: Docstring: Move data on a configured endpoint and wait for its transfer event. len must be exactly what the endpoint's protocol transfers: one HID report, or a whole number of 512-byte blocks. got receives the byte count only for the zero-length case, which is how a device reports "nothing new"; otherwise the transfer either completed at len or failed.
doc.description:
Returns 1 when the device completed the transfer, 0 on a stall, a transfer
error, or a timeout.

name: xhc_transfer_async
signature: int xhc_transfer_async(int index, int ep_index, void *buf, unsigned len)

doc.summary: Docstring: Post one endpoint transfer without waiting: the completion arrives on the event ring and is collected by xhc_poll_token.
doc.description: Returns the token, or 0 on refusal.

doc.summary: Docstring: Non-blocking completion check for xhc_transfer_async.
doc.description: Drains the ring, then reports 1 on success, -1 on a failed completion, -2 on a wait past the budget, and 0 while still outstanding. Consumed tokens are dropped, so a caller that polls to completion never leaks the table. A zero budget never expires: an interrupt endpoint with nothing to say answers NAK rather than an event, and expiring its only transfer orphans the report it eventually delivers to a token nobody holds.

doc.summary: Docstring: Reset, address, describe and register the device on a port.
doc.description: Returns its index, or -1 on any failure, in which case the slot is released and the error is counted. Idempotent per port: a port already holding a live device returns that device's index.

doc.summary: Docstring: Enumerate every port that has something attached.
doc.description: Returns the number of devices registered by this call.

doc.summary: Docstring: Bring up the first xHCI controller found.
doc.description: Returns 1 when a controller is running and xhc_poll will service it, 0 when there is none, which is the normal case on QEMU and on a machine whose firmware already owns the controller. Never leaves a half-mapped BAR behind: any failure restores the firmware's assignment.
